concept.name: Wyckoff redistribution
concept.definition: A consolidation within an ongoing downtrend in which remaining longs sell and large operators build or add to short positions before the markdown resumes. It mirrors reaccumulation on the downside and is identified only by the range's eventual downward resolution.
concept.intuition: During a bear market pause, hopeful buyers step in and the big players sell into that demand, restocking supply for the next leg down.
concept.mechanics: A redistribution range forms as a sideways pause during markdown; its Phase A may look like the start of accumulation (climactic action to the downside), but Phases B-E are analyzed like distribution, ending with signs of weakness and a break below range support that signals continuation of the downtrend.
concept.failure_modes: Redistribution is easily confused with accumulation bottoms in real time; bear-market rallies can extend far beyond the expected pause, and a labeled redistribution that breaks upward invalidates the interpretation.
concept.misconceptions: Every pause in a downtrend is not redistribution; without characteristic supply dominance (weak rallies, breakdowns on expanding volume), the range may be a genuine bottoming structure.
concept.example: Midway through a bear market, the index churns sideways for a month with volume rising on down days; the break below the consolidation low on expanding volume marks the range as redistribution and the downtrend resumes.

citations.source: The Wyckoff Method: A Tutorial (StockCharts.com ChartSchool, by Roman Bogomazov and Michael Lipsett)
citations.section: Distribution: Wyckoff Phases (Phase A); Accumulation: Wyckoff Phases (Phase E)
